analysis.title: Broadcom Inc.: Re-Sold TPU Racks Are Worth $35B Per GW
key_insights: A newly announced AI Compute Capacity SPV is worth $63B in aggregate, roughly $60B ex-fees. Sullivan and Cromwell's client highlight says the deal is a 1.7GW buildout, implying about $35B per GW.

Barclays' prior assumption for AVGO's $/GW was about $10B-$15B, covering chips and networking only. Grossed up for system architecture and other components, the portion of the value chain going to GOOGL did not make sense to the analysts.

First pass: chips plus networking at about $12.5B/GW midpoint, assumed to be roughly 80% of rack BOM, gives a total AI rack cost of about $15.6B. That leaves $19.38B of the $35B for GOOGL and others, which Barclays calls structurally far too high.

Revised view: with Google Cloud at a 35% margin, GOOGL's share is $12.25B, leaving $22.75B. Holding the 80% share constant, AVGO's chips plus networking $/GW comes to about $18.2B, which Barclays considers far more accurate.
Barclays estimates 11.3 total GWs deployed in CY27. At $18.2B/GW that gives CY27 AI revenue of about $205B vs Bloomberg Street AI revenue of about $138B.
For CY28 Barclays estimates about 22.6 potential GWs, implying about $410B of AI revenue vs Street CY28 AI revenue of about $256B.

External TPU total $/GW of $35B compares with NVDA Vera Rubin at about $40B/GW for AI systems, a discount of about 13%. Barclays is surprised the discount is so small, though $5B per GW is substantial savings on multi-GW deployments.

On its last earnings call AVGO pointed to 6.3GW for AI labs in CY27 and more than 15GW in CY28 of potential deployments. At $35B/GW that implies about $161B of spend in CY27 (excluding the 1.7GW already financed) and over $500B in CY28.
AVGO's backstop stepped down from 85% in the first agreement (June 9th) to 72.5% in the most recent one. Barclays expects future deals to lower the backstop further.

Credit view: negligible impact on AVGO credit quality, but chip-financing supply remains a serious overhang. Two financings totaling about $100bn have been placed through AVGO's XPV platform, with about $75bn of AVGO backstops.

Rating agencies and credit investors plan to add the backstops back onto Broadcom's balance sheet on a rateable basis tied to debt outstanding. Accelerating earnings and cash flow absorb most of the leverage effect, and agencies remain on Positive outlook.

Broadcom plans to deploy 20GW through the XPV through 2028. With rising $/GW on newer TPU pods, potential issuance could exceed the $500bn implied by the first transaction (Big Sky/APCHIP), alongside a separate $500bn Nvidia financing platform.
Barclays expects the chip-financing supply to compete for capital in the front end of AVGO's curve and keep weighing on spreads, with demand for AVGO CDS staying high on hedging activity.

market_movers.rationale: New SPV data implies much higher $/GW for AVGO than previously assumed, and Barclays' CY27 and CY28 AI revenue estimates sit well above Street. Price target is based on 22x CY27E EPS of $23.02.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays' industry view for the coverage universe is Neutral.

earnings_insights: Barclays estimates CY27 AI revenue of about $205B (estimate) vs Bloomberg Street AI revenue of about $138B (consensus).
Barclays estimates CY28 AI revenue of about $410B (estimate) vs Street CY28 AI revenue of about $256B (consensus).
Price target of $500 is based on 22x Barclays CY27E EPS of $23.02 (estimate).
risk_factors: Concentrated contingent exposure to certain AI labs through the backstops could amplify risk in an AI winter, though Barclays says this is far from its view.
Chip-financing debt supply could exceed $500bn from the XPV platform, alongside Nvidia's $500bn platform, adding to AI debt supply that has overwhelmed credit markets in 2026.
Rating agencies add backstops back to AVGO's balance sheet, and the adjustment is likely to grow with future deals.
vol_and_positioning: Demand for AVGO CDS is expected to remain high given potential hedging activity tied to chip-financing backstops.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays' revised $/GW of about $18.2B for AVGO chips and networking implies CY27 AI revenue of about $205B and CY28 of about $410B, well above Street.
tension_points.bear_case: Chip-financing supply, backstops added back to AVGO's balance sheet, and concentrated exposure to AI labs could pressure spreads and amplify risk in an AI downturn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Barclays expects the credit narrative to flip only when XPV chip financing slows and/or backstops decline materially; it does not call that yet.

theme_stances.key_argument: The SPV data implies a higher AVGO $/GW than previously assumed, so AI revenue forecasts sit well above Street.
Chip-financing debt supply remains a serious overhang for credit spreads even though AVGO credit quality is little affected.
